newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crude offerings to U.S. Gulf cheapening.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crude offerings to U.S. Gulf cheapening.

text.p: Foreign crude business to the United States Gulf continued to talk at cheap price levels Wednesday, although fresh deals were scarce for prompt barrels, cash traders said.

Sentiment continued to stay firmly on the bearish side, with most players saying despite recent upticks for very prompt domestic sweet supplies, the Gulf remained swamped with West African, North Sea Brent and Latin American offerings.
A buyer of Brent said a U.K. major was showing Brent for mid-April at May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing -60 cents.
Weak values in the Brent sector were apparent in the one confirmed wet deal, a March 26-28 loader at April Brent -90 cents, a shade lower than previous deals on Tuesday.

Latin crudes talked the same direction as Brent, with two so-called desperate sellers looking to unload Cano Limon cargoes. A trader said one of the Cano cargoes was talked at May WTI -$3.25 FOB for early April delivery to the U.S. Gulf.
The second, and more desperate of the pair, was offered at May WTI -$3.40 on a delivered basis for mid-April.
"These cargoes may not even sell, and could be pushed somewhere other than the Gulf," a Gulf crude buyer said.
"They may need to look at other strategies, we keep hearing the same thing that there is a lot of West African in the Gulf. It's not a good time to be a seller."
Qua Iboe was offered in the Gulf at May/WTI -20 cents for second decade April, traders added.
Other talk in the markets had Chile's ENAP prepared to put out a crude tender early next week, sources said.
U.S. aftermarket deals for paper Brent worked lower in a series of EFP (exchange for physicals) and cash outright partial trades.
More than a full cargo of paper Brent sold at $20.22 per barrel in May on an EFP basis, with another cargo going at $20.24 for cash, traders said.
Late U.S. numbers were 9-16 cents lower than the May IPE settlement at $20.33.
A trio of paper inter-month spreads saw April/May Brent move at plus 14 cents in two separate deals, and a May/July cargo at plus 23 cents.
